items.headline: Update: Singapore summons bosses of 10 firms as it widens its transboundary-haze probe
items.summary: Singapore ministers summoned the bosses of 10 locally registered companies potentially linked to the Indonesian wildfires behind weeks of record haze, widening an earlier inquiry into seven firms. Officials said the aim was 'not to find scapegoats' but to gather evidence as air quality lingered in the unhealthy range.

items.headline: Singapore presses gas suppliers to honour commitments after Indonesia cuts pipeline supply
items.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong urged gas suppliers to 'honour their commitments' after Indonesia trimmed piped-gas exports to Singapore, a dispute now tangled with the haze row. Wong said the government would explore nuclear power and widen energy partnerships to shore up supply.

items.headline: Haze-hit Singapore parents push for air-conditioning in schools
items.summary: With the Pollutant Standards Index stuck in the unhealthy range for weeks, some Singapore parents called for Hong Kong-style air-conditioning in schools as authorities handed out N95 masks to vulnerable residents. The Education Ministry said it could consider closures if forecasts turned hazardous.

items.headline: Elderly Chinese couple jailed in Singapore after overstaying about 19 years
items.summary: A 68-year-old woman was sentenced in Singapore to six months' jail and a S$2,000 fine in lieu of caning after overstaying for about 19 years, having turned herself in with her husband after struggling to get by. Her husband's case was listed for 29 October.

items.headline: Update: Cyclone Arnab makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh, killing at least three
items.summary: Cyclone Arnab came ashore in Andhra Pradesh on 28 October as a very severe cyclonic storm with winds near 135km/h, killing at least three people in the worst-hit state. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu reported at least 180 houses destroyed, and about 180,000 people were evacuated across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha before landfall.

items.headline: India's rupee stays under pressure near record lows as the RBI steps up its defence
items.summary: India's rupee has held near record lows against the US dollar in recent weeks, with strategists warning of a slide toward 100, even as the Reserve Bank of India tightened liquidity, curbed dollar demand, and raised its benchmark rate to 5.50%. Officials have pointed to the Middle East war and foreign outflows as pressures on the currency.

items.headline: Healey's Autumn Budget taxes banks and gambling, cuts energy bills and lifts defence
items.summary: Chancellor John Healey's first Autumn Budget, delivered on 28 October, leaned on banks, gambling, and vape shops to fund relief for households, cut energy bills, and raise defence spending. He said the money would come 'from those who can afford to pay', with no rise in taxes on wages or dividends.

items.headline: UK bank profit surcharge raised three points to 6% as gambling and vape duties rise
items.summary: Healey raised the bank profit surcharge by three percentage points to 6%, a temporary measure due to run for about 15 months from January, and increased gambling and gaming-machine duties. He framed the bank levy as a return of the support given after the financial crisis.

items.headline: Income tax on property and savings to rise two points, with no increase on wages or dividends
items.summary: Tax rates on income from property and savings will rise by a further two percentage points on top of increases already due in April 2027, while wages and dividends were spared. Healey also launched a 'Starter ISA' for first-time investors and scrapped a planned £12,000 cap on cash-ISA contributions.

items.headline: UK pledges to lift defence spending to 3.5% of GDP by 2035 and sends more aid to Ukraine
items.summary: Healey said he would fund a £15bn Defence Investment Plan and lift defence spending to 3.5% of GDP by 2035, plugging a £4.7bn gap by reprioritising other departments' budgets. He also pledged an extra £10bn in aid for Ukraine.

items.headline: OBR sees UK fiscal headroom cut to £15bn as gilt yields ease during Healey's speech
items.summary: The Office for Budget Responsibility put the Chancellor's fiscal headroom at about £15bn by 2029/30, down from £23.6bn in March, with the Middle East war cited as a drag. Markets stayed calm, as 10-year gilt yields eased from around 5.36% to 5.31% as Healey spoke.

items.headline: Update: Israel's election leaves Netanyahu and Eisenkot both short of a majority
items.summary: With most votes counted, Israel's 27 October election left both main blocs short of a majority: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp fell to about 53 seats, down from 68, while Gadi Eisenkot's bloc held about 48 and Arab-majority parties won a record 17 to 19. Neither can reach the 61 seats needed, and President Isaac Herzog will choose who tries first to form a government.

items.headline: Kremlin says Europe is excluded from next Ukraine talks as Zelenskyy sets Abu Dhabi dates
items.summary: The Kremlin said European countries would not take part in the next round of Ukraine peace talks, planned with the United States in Abu Dhabi, after a rare call with Nordic leaders. Speaking in The Hague, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the trilateral talks would run from 6 to 10 November and pressed for Europe to be included.

items.headline: Drone strike on Sudan's Nyala market kills at least 21 amid an escalating air campaign
items.summary: A drone strike on a market in Nyala, the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces' de facto capital in Sudan's Darfur region, killed at least 21 people and wounded 40, according to a medical source. It was part of an escalating wave of drone attacks that has killed more than 160 people across the country in recent days.

items.headline: UN inquiry says Israel is still committing genocide in Gaza despite the ceasefire
items.summary: A UN commission of inquiry said Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza despite the October 2025 ceasefire, pointing to killings of civilians near the 'Yellow Line', and accused Israel of crimes against humanity, including extermination, in the occupied West Bank. Israel's mission in Geneva rejected the report and called for the commission to be dissolved.

items.headline: Apple unveils a touchscreen MacBook Pro alongside an M6 iMac refresh
items.summary: Apple launched a touchscreen MacBook Pro, priced from $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch, with preorders opening 30 October and sales from 6 November. It followed a refresh a day earlier that put the new M6 chip in a 24-inch iMac and an entry 14-inch MacBook Pro.

items.headline: Nvidia releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free open speech-to-text model for 40 languages
items.summary: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free, open speech-to-text model that handles up to 40 languages, as it expands its push into voice AI. The launch adds to a run of open-weight model releases from the chipmaker this month.

items.headline: Nvidia backs Indian AI-inference startup Simplismart in a $14 million round
items.summary: Nvidia joined a $14 million Series B in Simplismart, an Indian startup whose software helps companies run AI models with fewer GPUs, valuing the four-year-old firm at about $100 million. Accel, Shastra VC, and Micromax also took part, with Dallas Venture Capital leading.

items.headline: Rivian buys UK startup Third Dimension to turn images into 3D worlds
items.summary: Electric-vehicle maker Rivian acquired Third Dimension, a UK startup founded by games and autonomous-vehicle veterans that uses AI to turn images and video into lifelike 3D worlds. Rivian framed the deal as support for its work on autonomy and spatial computing.

items.headline: US Federal Reserve holds rates in a 10-2 vote, keeping a December hike in play
items.summary: The US Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate in a range of 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote on 28 October, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favour of a hike. Chair Kevin Warsh said he did not believe in forward guidance, and traders still priced a December increase.

items.headline: Microsoft beats estimates as Azure revenue jumps 48%, lifting shares after hours
items.summary: Microsoft beat estimates for its fiscal first quarter, reporting revenue of about $92.3 billion, up 19%, as Azure revenue jumped 48%. Adjusted earnings of $4.89 a share topped forecasts, and the shares rose about 4% in extended trading.

items.headline: Alphabet's cloud revenue surges past $30 billion, but an equity loss dents its profit
items.summary: Alphabet's third-quarter revenue reached about $127.6 billion, with Google Cloud revenue surging roughly 90% to around $30.7 billion. Net income fell to about $26.2 billion, dragged down by an $8.7 billion loss on equity investments, a non-operating item.

items.headline: UPS beats quarterly estimates and raises its full-year guidance again
items.summary: United Parcel Service beat Wall Street expectations and again raised its full-year guidance, posting adjusted earnings of $1.69 a share on revenue of $22.9 billion. The company said it was cutting lower-margin Amazon deliveries, contributing to a 3.3% drop in US average daily volume.

items.headline: Nvidia and AMD to invest $4 billion in Meta as AI partnerships deepen
items.summary: Nvidia and AMD agreed to invest a combined $4 billion in Meta as part of the social-media company's roughly $95 billion capital raise, deepening ties between chipmakers and a major AI customer. The move extends a wave of cross-investment across the AI supply chain.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen and Norris among 10 drivers to sit out Mexico City first practice for rookies
items.summary: Max Verstappen, Lando Norris, and George Russell were among 10 drivers set to sit out first practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix on 30 October, with teams fielding rookies to meet a mandatory young-driver requirement. Mercedes reserve Frederik Vesti was named to take Russell's car.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli needs just two points in Mexico to clinch his first Formula 1 title
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli can clinch his first Formula 1 drivers' title at the Mexico City Grand Prix on 1 November, needing only a ninth-place finish, or for neither George Russell nor Lewis Hamilton to win. He leads Russell by 123 points with 125 still available, and Mercedes can also seal the constructors' crown.

items.headline: 🏏 India, 3-0 up, eye a 4-0 lead over New Zealand in the fourth T20I at Auckland
items.summary: India, already series winners at 3-0, aim to extend their lead to 4-0 against New Zealand in the fourth Twenty20 international at Eden Park, Auckland, on 30 October. Ishan Kishan remained an injury doubt after missing the previous two matches with an adductor strain.

items.headline: 🎾 Zverev closes on world No. 1 as the indoor swing reaches the Vienna quarter-finals
items.summary: Alexander Zverev, the top seed in Vienna, moved closer to the world No. 1 ranking as the Erste Bank Open reached the quarter-finals. Reaching the last eight would lift him above Jannik Sinner for the first time when the rankings update on 2 November.

items.headline: NASA's Swift telescope set to fall to Earth around 2 November after a failed rescue
items.summary: NASA's Swift gamma-ray space telescope is expected to re-enter Earth's atmosphere around 2 November after a private rescue failed, when a Katalyst spacecraft meant to boost its orbit spun out of control. NASA shut down Swift's science operations last week, and most of the two-decade-old observatory should burn up on re-entry.

items.headline: Europe's Hera probe resolves Didymos and Dimorphos as two asteroids for the first time
items.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft resolved Didymos and its moonlet Dimorphos as two separate objects for the first time, imaging the pair from about 1,280km away ahead of its arrival in November. Hera will survey Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA's DART mission struck in 2022 to test planetary defence.

items.headline: Landmark study estimates about three in four former NFL players died with CTE
items.summary: A study in JAMA Network Open estimated that about three in four former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 likely had chronic traumatic encephalopathy, based on records of 2,362 players. Among roughly 400 who donated their brains, 93.5% were found to have the disease, which can only be diagnosed after death.

items.headline: Physicists build a carbon nanoribbon of pentagons and heptagons that conducts like metal
items.summary: Physicists created a carbon nanoribbon built from alternating five- and seven-membered rings, rather than the usual hexagons, and found it conducts electricity like a metal. The structure could point toward new carbon-based electronic materials.

fun_fact.headline: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards
fun_fact.body: A hummingbird is the only kind of bird that can fly backwards, and even briefly upside down, thanks to a shoulder joint that lets its wings rotate almost 180 degrees and trace a figure-eight. In flight its wings can beat up to about 80 times a second, and its heart can race past 1,200 beats a minute.

puzzle.title: Out of the Blue
puzzle.body: A man is found dead in the middle of a wide, empty field, far from any road. There are no footprints or tyre tracks anywhere around him, no weapon, and no sign of a struggle. Beside him lies a small, closed pack. What happened to him?
puzzle.approach: Ask what the pack was for - and why it did not help him.
puzzle.answer: He was a parachutist (or BASE jumper). The small closed pack beside him is his parachute, which failed to open. He arrived from above, so there are no tracks leading to the body and no attacker; the only object with him is the pack that should have saved his life.

word_puzzle.title: Double Agents
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into four groups of four: PLANE, SWING, BUNKER, CAT, FILE, TWIST, ROUGH, SWORD, TAP, GREEN, JELLY, HAMMER, TEE, JIVE, STAR, DRILL.
word_puzzle.approach: A few words look at home in two groups - let the tightest set decide.
word_puzzle.answer: ___ FISH: CAT, SWORD, JELLY, STAR. TOOLS: HAMMER, DRILL, PLANE, FILE. DANCES: TAP, SWING, TWIST, JIVE. PARTS OF A GOLF COURSE: ROUGH, GREEN, BUNKER, TEE.

Only a subset of allowed outlets are reachable by the search crawler (Al Jazeera, CNN, CNBC, Bloomberg, TechCrunch, Nature, Scientific American, NASA/ESA, Sky Sports, ESPN, ATP, SCMP, Mothership); BBC, Reuters, AP, The Guardian, and the Indian/Singapore primary outlets (CNA, Straits Times, The Hindu, Indian Express, Times of India, NDTV, Hindustan Times, Economic Times) were not reachable.
UK News ran on the fallback tier (CNBC, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg) because BBC and Sky News were unreachable; the section is built from the delivered 28 Oct Autumn Budget.

India ran on the fallback tier (Al Jazeera, CNBC) after primary outlets were unreachable across 3+ retry attempts (FIX 6); fewer India stories cleared recency and sourcing today - the fresh Cyclone Arnab landfall plus the ongoing rupee/RBI macro story. The rupee item reflects a multi-week ongoing situation (source dated Oct 16).

Singapore leaned on the ongoing haze crisis (SCMP) plus one court item (Mothership); the haze is the dominant current SG story and prior-day haze items were excluded by dedup, so today's items cover distinct new facets (10-firm summons, gas-supply dispute, schools/masks).
Spectrum/bias blocks omitted this run: three distinct, verifiable left/center/right outlet framings could not be confirmed under the network constraints.

Puzzle type 'lateral' chosen as the next in the 4-type rotation (last used 2026-10-25); the strict 4-day window is degenerate with only four puzzle types, so the oldest-in-rotation was selected. Word puzzle type 'grouping' (last used 2026-10-24) is outside the 4-day word-puzzle exclusion.
